title: AI-Slop UI Anti-Patterns
description: Machine-readable catalog of AI-slop UI anti-patterns for finished product pages. Machine entries carry a DOM/CSS rule a headless-browser checker can implement and fail as errors; review entries carry a question for a human or agent reviewer and never gate.

measurement_context.browser: Headless Chromium, the same engine used for expression/measured-benchmarks.md and scripts/check-showcase.mjs.
measurement_context.viewport: 1440x900 CSS pixels, device scale factor 1, pointer: fine, prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference unless a rule says otherwise.
measurement_context.settling: Before measuring, scroll the document top to bottom in 450px steps with instant scrolling, waiting three animation frames per step so scroll-triggered reveals fire, return to the top, and await Promise.all(document.getAnimations().map((a) => a.finished)) with a 3000ms bound, skipping infinite animations. Never use a fixed sleep.
measurement_context.screen: A screen is one viewport-height slice of the document: scrollY = k * 900 for k = 0 .. ceil(scrollHeight / 900) - 1. Coverage percentages are the area of visible boxes intersected with the screen rectangle, divided by 1440 * 900, with overlapping boxes unioned.
measurement_context.visible: An element is visible when getClientRects().length > 0, its computed visibility is visible, its computed opacity and every ancestor's computed opacity are above 0, and its box intersects the screen being measured.
measurement_context.body_size: The character-weighted modal computed font-size, rounded to the nearest pixel, over all visible elements' own text nodes (the measured-benchmarks.md console method).
measurement_context.interactive: a[href], button, summary, [role=button], [role=link], [role=tab], input[type=button], input[type=submit], excluding elements with the disabled attribute or aria-disabled=true.

profiles.detection: stylegallery audit check resolves the profile before checking: an explicit --profile wins; otherwise app when the page declares role=application or shows 3 or more form controls on at most 2 screens with links under 60% of the text, content when links carry at least 70% of the rendered text, or at least 60% with at most 3 content images, or when the page has no content imagery and at least 1500 characters of text, and landing otherwise. The resolved profile, its source, and the signals are reported.

landing.description: A marketing, brand, or product landing page: the finished-page surface the 49 measured originals represent.
landing.rationale: Every rule in this catalog was calibrated on landing and brand homepages (expression/measured-benchmarks.md), so all machine rules are errors.

app.description: A product or tool surface: dashboards, editors, search and booking forms, signed-in views.
app.rationale: Richness floors, display scale, surface finishing, and motion density were measured on landing pages; application surfaces trade them for density and stability, so these rules become warnings. Accessibility checks, honest actions, emoji icons, unanchored violet gradients, and soft shadows stay errors.

content.description: A reading or index surface: articles, documentation, government and news pages, link directories.
content.rationale: Text-led pages are finished by their text, not by imagery: GOV.UK screens of 8.5% and 9.9% text and Hacker News links without hover transitions are correct for their purpose, yet missed the landing floors in the 2026-10-19 real-site run. Landing-only rules become warnings; accessibility checks and honest actions stay errors.

entries.title: Headline alone on a gradient screen
entries.definition: A screen whose only content is a heading, and perhaps a short line and a button, set over a gradient or flat fill, with no picture, drawn scene, render, live product surface, or dense text.

detection.scope: Every screen of every page.
detection.measure: For each screen: media_coverage = unioned area of visible img, picture, video, canvas, svg elements at least 120x80, elements whose computed background-image contains url(, and [data-surface] elements; text_coverage = unioned area of the client rects of visible text-node ranges; heading_present = a visible h1, h2, or h3, or a text run at least 2.5x body_size, intersects the screen; gradient_ground = the topmost box behind the screen centre, or any element covering at least 50% of the screen, has a computed background-image containing gradient(.
detection.threshold: media_coverage < 8% and text_coverage < 10%, the same floors as showcase/QA.md Q22.
detection.violation: One error per screen where heading_present is true, both coverage floors are missed, and gradient_ground is true. A screen that misses both floors without a gradient ground is reported by slop.empty-screen instead. Screens held by a pinned (sticky) scene are skipped, as in slop.empty-screen.

entries.rationale: The 49 measured originals give a median 53% of page area to raster images, video, and background images and only 3.9% to gradients; the studies gave 0% to imagery and 26% to gradients, which is why whole sections read empty (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 1). showcase/QA.md I16 forbids a headline alone on a gradient.

entries.title: Empty screen
entries.definition: A screen that shows neither imagery nor enough text, whatever its background.

detection.scope: Every screen of every page except the last screen when it is shorter than 450px. A screen at least half covered by the containing block of a sticky element that holds text or media is skipped: the pinned scene fills it as the reader scrolls.
detection.measure: media_coverage and text_coverage as defined in slop.headline-only-gradient-screen.
detection.threshold: media_coverage < 8% and text_coverage < 10%.
detection.violation: One error per screen that misses both floors and is not already reported as slop.headline-only-gradient-screen.

entries.rationale: showcase/QA.md I16 and Q22 require at least 8% media or 10% text on every screen. expression/measured-benchmarks.md treats imagery as the floor for a finished page: a page with no raster or rendered imagery reads as a wireframe regardless of palette.

entries.title: Random purple gradient
entries.definition: A large blue-violet-to-magenta gradient whose hue appears nowhere else in the page's solid colors, so it signals a default rather than a brand.

detection.scope: Every visible element with a computed background-image containing linear-gradient(, radial-gradient(, or conic-gradient(, including repeating forms.
detection.measure: Parse each gradient's color stops to HSL. violet_stops = stops with hue in [245deg, 320deg], saturation >= 35%, and alpha >= 0.3. painted_share = unioned area of such elements on a screen divided by the screen area. anchor_hues = hues of every visible element's solid computed color, background-color, border-*-color, and outline-color with saturation >= 35% and alpha >= 0.3, excluding gradients.
detection.threshold: At least 2 violet_stops in one gradient, painted_share >= 15% on any screen, and no anchor hue within 20deg of any violet stop.
detection.violation: One error per gradient element that meets all three conditions.

entries.rationale: Gradient-painted area is 3.9% of the median original and 26% of the median study (expression/measured-benchmarks.md); the rule fires only when a violet gradient is both large and disconnected from every solid brand color, which separates a default from a chosen accent.

entries.title: Gradient filling the space imagery should hold
entries.definition: Gradients paint more of the page than the measured originals' upper quartile, standing in for content.

detection.scope: The whole page.
detection.measure: gradient_share = sum over screens of the unioned area of visible elements whose computed background-image contains gradient(, divided by the sum of screen areas. Elements with a computed mask-image or clip-path other than none that are smaller than 25% of a screen are excluded, because edge fades and vignettes are finishing detail, not fill.
detection.threshold: gradient_share > 17%, the p75 of the 49 originals.
detection.violation: One error per page.

entries.rationale: Originals paint 0 / 3.9% / 17% (p25 / median / p75) of their area with gradients; the studies' median of 26% sits above the originals' p75 and was diagnosed as gradients filling the space imagery should hold (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 1).

entries.title: Excessive soft shadows
entries.definition: Cards and panels separated by large blurred drop shadows instead of masks, clips, and hairlines.

detection.scope: Every visible element on the page.
detection.measure: soft_shadowed = elements whose computed box-shadow has at least one non-inset layer with blur radius >= 24px and alpha > 0, excluding elements that float by role: [role=dialog], [role=menu], [role=listbox], [role=tooltip], [aria-modal=true], dialog[open], [popover]:popover-open, and their descendants.
detection.threshold: soft_shadowed count > 1. The originals' median is 0 and p75 is 1.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing each soft-shadowed element's selector.

entries.rationale: Elements with 24px+ blur shadows: originals 0 / 0 / 1 (p25 / median / p75), studies median 2. The originals finish surfaces with a median 12 masked or clipped elements and 24 hairlines instead (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 3; expression/techniques/surface-detail.md).

entries.title: No masks, clips, or hairlines
entries.definition: Surfaces with no mask, rounded clip, or 1px rule, the finishing detail the measured originals use instead of shadows.

detection.scope: The whole page.
detection.measure: masked = visible elements with computed mask-image (or -webkit-mask-image) other than none, or clip-path other than none; hairlines = visible elements with at least one border side whose computed width is exactly 1px and style is not none.
detection.threshold: masked < 2 or hairlines < 3, the showcase/QA.md Q24 floor.
detection.violation: One error per page.

entries.rationale: Originals: masked or clipped elements 1 / 12 / 27 and 1px borders 3 / 24 / 65 (p25 / median / p75); studies had 0 and 13 (expression/measured-benchmarks.md). showcase/QA.md I18 and Q24 set the floor at 2 and 3.

entries.title: Emoji used as icons
entries.definition: Emoji characters standing in for icons in navigation, buttons, headings, list markers, or feature cards.

detection.scope: Visible elements matching nav *, button, a, li, h1-h6, [role=tab], and any child of a grid or flex container with 3 or more siblings that share its tag name.
detection.measure: Split each element's own trimmed text into grapheme clusters with Intl.Segmenter. An emoji grapheme matches /\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u and is not one of the text symbols U+00A9, U+00AE, U+2122, U+2190-U+21FF, U+2713, U+2714. icon_use = the element's whole own text is 1-2 emoji graphemes, or its own text begins with an emoji grapheme followed by whitespace.
detection.threshold: 2 or more icon_use elements on a page.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing every icon_use element.

entries.rationale: Emoji render differently on every platform and announce as their Unicode names to screen readers. The measured originals use raster imagery, drawn vectors, or product surfaces on every screen (expression/measured-benchmarks.md; expression/techniques/drawn-products.md), and showcase/QA.md I16 counts only pictures, drawn scenes, renders, and live surfaces as content.

entries.title: Repeated identical three-card grids
entries.definition: Two or more rows of three or four structurally identical, imageless cards (icon, heading, sentence), the template feature grid.

detection.scope: Every visible element whose computed display is grid, inline-grid, flex, or inline-flex.
detection.measure: A triplet is a container whose visible element children number 3 or 4, share one top edge within 4px, have widths within 2px of each other, contain no visible img, picture, video, or canvas, and have an identical signature, where signature = the ordered list of descendant tag names (svg subtrees collapsed to svg, text-only inline elements ignored).
detection.threshold: 2 or more triplets on a page whose children share one signature, or 3 or more triplets with any signatures. A single row also fails when every card is at least 160x120px, is not itself a button or tab, and opens with a drawn icon (svg at most 64x64px) before its heading or text.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing each triplet container.

entries.rationale: Originals put pictures in every card and change pace down a 9.1-viewport page; studies compressed to 4.4 viewports and gave each idea one short beat (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gaps 1 and 5). A repeated imageless triplet is the clearest machine signature of that compression and of a missing picture on the screen (showcase/QA.md I16). The taste-skill study (model panel) found rows of icon-topped identical cards on 7% of top-scored and 26% of bottom-scored sites, which is why one such row is enough.

entries.title: Links and buttons without a state change
entries.definition: Links, buttons, tabs, or cards that do not change at all under the pointer or keyboard focus.

detection.scope: Every visible interactive element (measurement_context.interactive) at 1440x900 with pointer: fine. Elements that are zero-size or at most 1px, outside the document, clipped by an overflow ancestor or a clip, inside [aria-hidden=true] or [inert], or under a hidden ancestor are skipped and counted in evidence.skipped, never reported. Live pages (stylegallery audit check) sample at most 24 elements evenly across the document.
detection.measure: Snapshot computed color, background-color, background-image, border-*-color, outline-style, outline-color, text-decoration-line, text-decoration-color, opacity, transform, translate, scale, box-shadow, filter, and clip-path on the element and its descendants up to depth 2. Then hover the element with the pointer and await its getAnimations({ subtree: true }) finished promises (bounded at 1000ms); snapshot again. Then move the pointer away, focus the element with the keyboard (Tab order), and snapshot a third time.
detection.threshold: 0 changed properties between the rest and hover snapshots, or 0 changed properties between the rest and focus snapshots; 1 such element is enough to fail the page.
detection.violation: One error per element, reported as hover_unchanged, focus_unchanged, or focus_unreachable (the complete Tab walk never reached it). An element the pointer cannot reach (hover times out) or that a capped Tab walk did not reach is skipped, not a violation.

entries.rationale: Originals put transitions on a median 76 elements per page, mostly opacity, color, transform, and background-color; studies had 8 and felt static (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 4). showcase/QA.md I17 requires links, buttons, cards, tabs, and media frames to change state under the pointer, and I6 requires every focused element to be visible.

entries.title: Sluggish or sparse state transitions
entries.definition: State changes that run longer than the measured 100-320ms band, or too few responding elements for the page length.

detection.scope: The whole page.
detection.measure: durations = for each visible a[href] and button with a computed transition-duration above 0, the longest duration among transitioned properties other than all-with-0s; transitioning = count of visible elements with any computed transition-duration above 0; viewports = scrollHeight / 900.
detection.threshold: median(durations) > 350ms, or median(durations) < 100ms, or transitioning < max(12, 4 * viewports). The 350ms and count floors are showcase/QA.md Q23; the 100ms lower edge is the measured band.
detection.violation: One error per page naming which bound failed (reasons speed and too_few). When slop.static-interactive also fails, only the speed reason is reported: controls that do not respond at all are one finding, not two.

entries.rationale: Hover and state transitions on the originals run 100-320ms, with a median dominant duration of 200ms; studies used 400ms and felt sluggish (expression/measured-benchmarks.md). showcase/QA.md Q23 fails a page whose median link and button duration exceeds 350ms or that has fewer than 4 transitioning elements per screen of length.

entries.title: Fake or dishonest call to action
entries.definition: A call to action that looks real but does nothing, jumps to the top, or pretends to complete an action that does not exist.

detection.scope: Visible interactive elements that are not skip links (/^skip (to|navigation)/i and Korean equivalents), consent or cookie controls (inside an element whose id, class, or aria-label names cookie, consent, onetrust, gdpr, or cmp, or whose name mentions cookies or consent), or legal links (privacy, terms, legal, imprint, accessibility statement), outside header and footer, plus every such element in header or footer whose accessible name matches /\b(get started|sign ?up|subscribe|book|buy|order|download|try|start|join|request|contact|get (a|an|the|your)|claim|reserve)\b/i.
detection.measure: Static: href is empty, #, #top, or javascript:, or href is #id with no element of that id. Dynamic: record location.href, scrollY, open dialogs, the text of [role=status], [role=alert], and [aria-live] regions, aria-expanded, aria-selected, and aria-pressed states, the rendered body text, and outgoing requests; activate the element with a click; await one animation frame and the element's animations (bounded at 1000ms); record again.
detection.threshold: 1 or more elements with a static match, or with 0 of these effects after activation: a URL change, a request, a newly open dialog or popover, an existing hash target scrolled into the top half of the viewport, or new non-empty text in a status, alert, or live region, a changed aria-expanded, aria-selected, or aria-pressed state, changed rendered text, or a scroll of more than 40px. A click that times out is skipped as unreachable, not a violation. Live pages sample at most 8 calls to action.
detection.violation: One error per element. A fictional action that announces itself in a role=status message passes, as showcase/QA.md I2 and Q4 require.

entries.rationale: showcase/QA.md I2 requires every link and button to do something plausible and fictional actions to say so in an announced status message; Q3 forbids # and #top targets and Q4 requires the status message without a scroll jump. expression/techniques/live-product-demos.md asks demos to answer honestly.

entries.title: Oversized display type
entries.definition: Display type so large relative to the body that it shouts, crowding out imagery and pacing.

detection.scope: All visible text on the page, measured at 1440x900.
detection.measure: body = body_size; display = the largest computed font-size among visible elements with own text; ratio = display / body; display_share = characters set at >= 2.5 * body divided by all visible characters.
detection.threshold: ratio > 5.5, the originals' p75, or display_share > 8.2%, the originals' p75.
detection.violation: One error per page naming ratio and display_share. A ratio below 3.5 is not an error: Korean service originals run near 2.0 by design.

entries.rationale: Largest size over body size on the originals: 2.8 / 3.95 / 5.5 (p25 / median / p75); studies median 5.2 with 22 of 49 studies more than 20% higher. Display share: originals 0.4% / 4.7% / 8.2%, studies 8.6% (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 2). AGENTS.md and expression/techniques/display-type-calibration.md set display type at 3.5-5.5 times the body.

entries.title: Generic marketing copy
entries.definition: Headlines and section copy that could sit on any product: unlock, supercharge, seamless, next-level, all-in-one, built for the future.
entries.review_question: If the product name were removed, could a reader tell from the headline and the first paragraph what this product does, for whom, and what is different about it?
entries.rationale: Word lists produce false positives on honest copy, so this stays a review question. The measured originals spend expression on content and response rather than on claims (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, Opinionated Guidance), and expression/direction-brief.md asks for a copy register chosen per direction.

entries.title: Fabricated social proof
entries.definition: Invented customer logos, testimonials, ratings, user counts, or metrics presented as real.
entries.review_question: Is every logo, quote, rating, and number on the page either sourced, or visibly marked as illustrative in a study or demo?
entries.rationale: showcase/QA.md I2 requires fictional actions to say they are fictional; the same honesty applies to claims. expression/brand-studies.md forbids copied logos and verbatim copy and requires an Unofficial mark on brand studies.

entries.title: Gradient text as the default emphasis
entries.definition: background-clip: text gradients applied to headings and numbers as the page's main way of adding emphasis.

detection.scope: Every visible element whose own subtree holds text.
detection.measure: gradient_text = elements whose computed background-clip (or -webkit-background-clip) is text and whose background-image contains gradient(.
detection.threshold: 2 or more gradient_text elements on a page.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing each element. A single gradient wordmark or display line passes.

entries.rationale: Gradient text is easy to count but its fit depends on the direction, so it is a review question rather than a gate. Studies already painted six times more gradient area than the originals (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 1); expression/techniques/display-type-calibration.md asks display type to read confident, not loud. The taste-skill study (model panel) found gradient text on 2% of top-scored and 13% of bottom-scored sites, so the rule is machine-checked; one gradient wordmark or display line remains allowed.

entries.title: Uniform section rhythm
entries.definition: Every section has the same height, the same centered heading-plus-subtitle opener, and the same background change, so the page has no pacing.
entries.review_question: Do the sections differ in length, density, and opener so that the page has a paced sequence rather than a stack of equal beats?
entries.rationale: Originals run 9.1 viewports with a median of 3 background band changes; studies ran 4.4 viewports with 6 band changes, giving each idea a single short beat (expression/measured-benchmarks.md, gap 5). Rhythm needs judgment, so this stays a review question.

entries.title: Eyebrow labels over every heading
entries.definition: Small, tracked, all-capital labels set directly above headings across the page, a template device that announces each section instead of letting the heading do it.

detection.scope: Visible elements outside headings, nav, header, footer, buttons, and labels whose own text is at most 40 characters.
detection.measure: small_caps = elements whose computed font-size is at most 13.5px, whose text is set in capitals (text-transform: uppercase, or own text equal to its upper-case form with at least one capital letter), and whose computed letter-spacing is at least 0.05em. An eyebrow is a small_caps element with an h1, h2, h3, [role=heading], or a text run at least 2.5x body_size starting 0-48px below its bottom edge and overlapping it horizontally.
detection.threshold: 3 or more eyebrows on a page.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing each eyebrow's selector and text.

entries.rationale: In the taste-skill study (model panel) of 247 gallery sites, three or more small-caps labels appeared on 6% of the top-scored sites and 43% of the bottom-scored sites. The study notes its own detector over-counts, so the rule requires the label to sit directly on a heading and three such labels before it fails; one or two kickers remain allowed. Relaxed to a warning for app and content pages.

entries.title: Pill badge above the headline
entries.definition: A small rounded pill ("New", "Beta", an announcement) placed directly above a headline as a kicker.

detection.scope: Visible elements outside nav, header, and footer whose own text is at most 30 characters.
detection.measure: pill = an element 16-40px tall whose computed border-top-left-radius is at least half its height minus 1px and that paints a background with alpha above 0.05 or a top border. A kicker is a pill with an h1, h2, h3, [role=heading], or a text run at least 2.5x body_size starting 0-48px below it and overlapping it horizontally.
detection.threshold: 1 or more kickers on a page.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing each kicker.

entries.rationale: The taste-skill study (model panel) found headline pill badges on 5% of top-scored and 26% of bottom-scored sites. Relaxed to a warning for app and content pages, where status pills above titles are functional.

entries.title: Lopsided page frame
entries.definition: Most content frames sit closer to one edge of the viewport than the other, so the page reads as shifted rather than composed.

detection.scope: Content elements (own text, outside header, nav, footer, and dialogs) at 1440x900.
detection.measure: frame = the outermost ancestor of a content element that is narrower than the viewport (stopping at full-width bands; frames inside fixed elements are ignored). For each distinct frame inside the viewport, left gutter = its left edge and right gutter = 1440 minus its right edge.
detection.threshold: At least 3 frames, and 60% or more of them lean the same way by more than 16px (one gutter exceeds the other by more than 16px).
detection.violation: One error per page, naming the side and a sample of leaning frames.

entries.rationale: The taste-skill study (model panel) second study of 100 Awwwards sites of the day found strong pages keep their outer left and right margins within a few pixels. A left-aligned measure inside a centred page is normal, so the rule counts frames and fails only when most of them lean the same way; live checks of Linear, Apple, and Notion stay clean. Relaxed for app and content pages.

entries.title: Half-empty screen
entries.definition: A screen whose text and media all sit in one half of the viewport while the other half holds nothing.

detection.scope: Every screen at least 450px tall at 1440x900.
detection.measure: For each screen with text_coverage of at least 2%: every text line box and media box with a layout box and computed visibility visible (whatever its opacity) that intersects the screen lies within x <= 720, or every one lies within x >= 720. Screens held by a pinned (sticky) scene are skipped.
detection.threshold: 1 or more such screens.
detection.violation: One error per screen, naming the side.

entries.rationale: The taste-skill study (model panel) second study found a section with text in one half and the other half empty on roughly 1 of 100 strong pages. Content pages with a single reading column are expected to do this, so the rule is a warning for content and app pages.

entries.title: Dead vertical gap
entries.definition: A vertical band longer than two thirds of a screen with no text and no media between two pieces of content.

detection.scope: The whole document at 1440x900, after the settling scroll.
detection.measure: Content spans = the vertical extents of every text line box and media box that has a layout box and computed visibility visible, whatever its opacity (reveal-on-scroll content holds its place). Walk the spans in order of their top edge, tracking the lowest bottom edge reached so far. The containing block of a sticky element with text or media counts as one content span.
detection.threshold: A span that starts more than 600px (two thirds of the 900px screen) below the lowest bottom edge reached before it.
detection.violation: One error per gap, with its start, end, and length. Space after the last content is not a gap.

entries.rationale: The taste-skill study (model panel) second study flags blank bands longer than half a screen as a usability cost. Live checks found 450-550px spacing bands on GitHub, Stripe, and Linear, so the threshold here is two thirds of a screen; slop.empty-screen measures coverage per fixed screen and can miss a gap that straddles two screens. Relaxed for app and content pages.

entries.title: First screen without a title
entries.definition: The first screen has no h1, so the page never states what it is in its document structure.

detection.scope: The first screen (0-900px) at 1440x900.
detection.measure: h1 boxes = h1 and [role=heading][aria-level=1] elements with text, a layout box, and computed visibility visible, including visually hidden (1px) headings, which still state the page in its structure.
detection.threshold: 0 h1 boxes intersecting the first screen.
detection.violation: One error per page, with the page's total h1 count.

entries.rationale: In the taste-skill study (model panel) second study, 15 of 97 first screens did not say what the site was and scored lower on usability; a first-screen h1 is the machine-visible half of that. Link directories and portals often omit it, so the rule is a warning for content and app pages.

entries.title: Sections without headings
entries.definition: Text-bearing sections with no heading, so a scanning reader cannot tell where one topic ends and the next begins.

detection.scope: section, article, and [role=region] elements outside header, nav, footer, aside, and dialogs.
detection.measure: untitled = such elements whose rendered text is at least 200 characters and that contain no h1-h6 or [role=heading].
detection.threshold: 2 or more untitled sections on a page.
detection.violation: One error per page, listing each untitled section.

entries.rationale: The taste-skill study (model panel) second study found 82% of text sections on strong pages open with a heading. One untitled section is common (a quote, a legal note), so two are required. Relaxed for app and content pages.

entries.title: First screen blocked after load
entries.definition: 4.5 seconds after load, a preloader or entry gate still covers the first screen, its text is still invisible, or a wheel turn does not move the page.

detection.scope: The first screen at 1440x900, measured 4.5 seconds after the load event and before any scrolling.
detection.measure: overlay = a fixed or absolutely positioned element with opacity above 0.5 that paints a background (alpha at least 0.5, an image, or a backdrop filter), covers at least 90% of the viewport, is the topmost element at the viewport centre, is not a dialog, and does not contain the h1. hidden_text = an h1 or h2 intersecting the first screen, outside header, nav, footer, menus, dialogs, [hidden], and [aria-hidden=true], whose effective opacity (product over ancestors) is below 0.1 or whose visibility is hidden. wheel_blocked = on a document taller than 1.5 screens, a 600px wheel turn at the viewport centre moves neither the document nor any inner scroller by 40px within 1500ms.
detection.threshold: 1 or more overlay, hidden_text, or wheel_blocked findings.
detection.violation: One error per finding, with its reason and selector.

entries.rationale: The taste-skill study (model panel) second study found preloaders on 60 of 99 award sites, wheel hijacking associated with lower usability scores (6.01 against 6.50), and first-screen text left at 0 opacity; motion/usability-anti-patterns.md rewrites the guidance. Blocking the first screen is a usability failure on every page type, so the rule stays an error in every profile.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Ban monospace outside code
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: The taste-skill study (model panel) reports monospace labels on 44% of strong sites versus 24% of weak sites. Its ban is a house preference, not evidence of inferior design.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Ban zero-padded section numbers
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: The taste-skill study (model panel) reports index numbers on 38% of strong sites versus 21% of weak sites. Review whether numbering communicates order instead of banning 01/02.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Ban hairlines and 1px boxes
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: The taste-skill study (model panel) reports thin rules on 61% of strong sites versus 52% of weak sites, without a useful negative distinction. Our measured originals use a median 24 hairlines; a ban conflicts with our surface guidance.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Fail every headline longer than two lines
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: In the taste-skill study (model panel), 71% of strong sites and 83% of weak sites meet the desktop two-line condition. This does not justify an error threshold across languages and widths.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Always size display type at 8.4vw
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: The 8.4vw figure is a strong-site median in the taste-skill study (model panel), not a universal prescription. Its gallery sample differs from our originals; preserve our body-relative calibration and direction-specific exceptions.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Ban Claude-brand hex values and cream with terracotta
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: A brand-associated palette is not evidence of poor usability or composition. Color selection needs the brief, contrast, and product context, not a brand blacklist.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Turn a cliche-word dictionary into build errors
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: Words alone cannot distinguish a concrete product claim from filler. Keep copy specificity as contextual review rather than a lexical error.

reviewed_and_rejected.title: Import model-laziness research and prompting prescriptions
reviewed_and_rejected.reason: Model motivation and incentive claims lack a locally verified basis and fall outside this design catalog's evidence boundary. No prompting prescriptions or research material are admitted.
